title: Jemimah Rodrigues Ruled Out of The Hundred, Asia Cup Participation in Doubt
excerpt: India batter suffers hamstring injury while playing for Southern Brave, raising concerns about her availability for the Women's T20 Asia Cup starting August 28.
body:
• Jemimah Rodrigues has been ruled out of The Hundred after suffering a hamstring injury while playing for Southern Brave
  • Her participation in the Women's T20 Asia Cup, starting August 28 in Dubai, is now in serious doubt
  • Rodrigues scored 143 runs in six innings at an average of 35.75 with two Player of the Match awards before the injury
  • If she fails to recover in time, Yastika Bhatia could be called up as a replacement in the Indian squad

India batter Jemimah Rodrigues has been ruled out of the remainder of The Hundred after suffering a hamstring injury while playing for Southern Brave, casting serious doubt over her participation in the upcoming Women's T20 Asia Cup and the Asian Games.

Southern Brave confirmed the injury on August 8, signing Australian all-rounder Charli Knott as Rodrigues' replacement for the rest of the tournament.

"We can confirm that due to an injury suffered by Jemimah Rodrigues, we've signed Charli Knott as our injury replacement for the remainder of The Hundred. Wishing you a speedy recovery, Jemi."

— Southern Brave, official statement

A Campaign Cut Short

Rodrigues had been in impressive form for Southern Brave in the 100-ball competition, scoring 143 runs in six innings at an average of 35.75 and a strike rate of 131.19, with a highest score of 42 not out. She earned two Player of the Match awards and was instrumental in Southern Brave's push toward the knockout stages. The team sits second on the points table with five wins from six matches and 20 points.

The 25-year-old had been signed as a direct pick for £60,000 (approximately $80,000), reflecting her status as one of the premier batters in women's cricket globally.

Asia Cup and Asian Games at Risk

The bigger concern for Indian cricket is Rodrigues' availability for the Women's T20 Asia Cup, scheduled from August 28 to September 13 in Dubai. India begin their Group A campaign against Thailand on August 30, followed by matches against Hong Kong on September 3 and arch-rivals Pakistan on September 5. All matches will be played at the Dubai International Stadium.

With less than three weeks between the injury and India's opening match, the timeline for recovery is tight. The extent of the hamstring injury has not been publicly disclosed, and her withdrawal from The Hundred could be a precautionary measure to preserve her fitness for national duty.

Beyond the Asia Cup, the injury also threatens her participation in the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, scheduled for September 17-22. India are the defending champions, having won gold in Hangzhou in 2023 by defeating Sri Lanka in the final.

Replacement Options

If Rodrigues is unable to recover in time, the Indian selectors may turn to Yastika Bhatia, who was left out of both the Asia Cup and Asian Games squads despite scoring a century in the Lord's Test. Wicketkeeper-batter G. Kamalini, the 18-year-old who replaced Yastika in the Asian Games squad, is another option already in the setup.

Rodrigues, known for her ability to manipulate pace and spin and accelerate during the middle overs, played an important role in India's ICC Women's ODI World Cup victory in 2025. India are the most successful team in Asia Cup history, with four ODI and three T20I format titles. Her absence would leave a significant gap in the middle order at a critical stretch of the international calendar.
